name: Mixed Functioning Pituitary Adenoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Endocrine Society Pituitary Adenoma Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Evidence of secretion of two or more pituitary hormones confirmed by biochemical assays
MRI demonstrating pituitary adenoma with characteristic features
Immunohistochemical staining confirming multiple hormone production in tumor cells
Presence of clinical signs and symptoms attributable to excess secretion of multiple pituitary hormones

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pituitary adenoma on imaging plus biochemical evidence of secretion of two or more pituitary hormones confirmed by histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, imaging, and histopathological data.

pathognomonic.notes: Combination of prolactin and growth hormone excess symptoms

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visual field defects due to optic chiasm compression
searchTerms: loss of side vision from optic pressure
visual field loss due to nerve compression
tunnel vision from optic chiasm pressure

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated serum insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) with hyperprolactinemia
pathognomonic.notes: Biochemical hallmark of mixed hormone secretion
searchTerms: elevated growth factor and hormone levels
increased insulin-like growth factor with prolactin

common.symptomName: Headache related to pituitary mass effect
searchTerms: head pain due to pituitary swelling

occasional.symptomName: Hypopituitarism symptoms due to mass effect

searchTerms: blood pressure increase from endocrine causes

occasional.symptomName: Mood disturbances including depression or anxiety

rare.symptomName: Cranial nerve palsies due to cavernous sinus invasion
searchTerms: cranial nerve weakness from tumor spread
nerve palsies due to cavernous sinus invasion

laboratory: Elevated serum prolactin and growth hormone levels
Abnormal pituitary hormone panel showing multiple hormone excess
imaging: MRI showing pituitary macroadenoma with suprasellar extension
Compression of optic chiasm on imaging
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence common
other: Histopathology demonstrating plurihormonal adenoma cells via immunohistochemistry

distinguishingFeatures: Secretion of prolactin only without other hormone excess
Exclusive growth hormone excess without prolactin or other hormone secretion
No biochemical evidence of hormone hypersecretion
Symptoms mainly due to mass effect

redFlags: Rapid visual field loss or sudden vision impairment
Severe headache with nausea and vomiting indicating possible apoplexy
Signs of acute hypopituitarism or adrenal crisis
references: Melmed S. Pituitary Tumors. Endocrinology: Adult and Pediatric. 7th ed. 2016.
Orphanet: Mixed Functioning Pituitary Adenoma. ORPHA:314759.
